thread:
nora: POC customer reporting 401 then 403 on /v1/generate. They rotated keys and see inconsistent behavior. Can we triage?

diego: Can you grab the exact curl and response body? 401 -> 403 usually key invalid -> scope/org mismatch.

nora: They sent this (key redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-foo' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Org: acme-inc' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rl2","input":"ping"}'
```
Response: `{"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid api key"}` then later `{"error":"forbidden","message":"org mismatch: token_org=acme-staging, header_org=acme-inc"}`

eva: Logs show token sk-poc-foo was rotated in their CI to a staging key. After rotation the key validated but bound to `acme-staging`. Header is `acme-inc`. That's the mismatch.

nora: I told them header doesn't override binding. They asked why header exists at all.

sam: Header is used in some multi-tenant routing cases but it cannot escalate privileges. Token binding is authoritative for authZ. We'll give the customer a one-pager for their security review.

diego: Also check scopes. If the token only has `embeddings` scope, /generate will 403 even if org matches. Ask them to run `/v1/whoami`.

eva: Sent customer this command: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-poc-foo" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/whoami`

nora: They returned: `{"org":"acme-staging","project":"demo-7","scopes":["embeddings:read"]}`

sam: There's the issue: only embeddings:read. For generate they need `generate` or `generate:write`. For POC recommend `generate,embeddings` combined scope.

diego: They also got a handful of 429s when their test runner retried on 401. support-bot shows a small spike.

support-bot: alert: 429 rate_limit_exceeded for acme-inc - burst detected, retry-after: 10s

eva: Explain exponential backoff and pausing the runner. They should stop the loop and re-run slowly.

nora: Customer asked if we can issue a temporary cross-org POC token to avoid rotating their CI keys. Also asked about POC credits/pricing impact.

sam: We can mint a scoped POC token (e.g., 200k tokens, 150 RPM) time-limited. Usage within agreed POC quota is covered by AE; anything over we bill unless sales ops approves.

diego: Action items for swarm: 1) Ask them to pause runner; 2) run whoami and paste output; 3) either remove X-Redwood-Org header or use a token bound to the target org; 4) request temp POC token if needed; 5) provide security one-pager.

eva: I'll draft the one-pager with: token binding semantics, whoami example, sample log lines showing token->org, audit log retention (90 days for POC), and KMS options.

nora: I sent the checklist and offered a temp token. They accepted a 7-day token at 200k tokens and 200 RPM, AE to log in deal notes.

support-bot: note: rate spike subsided for acme-inc

diego: They swapped to the temp token and re-ran tests. 401/403 cleared, only 1-2 transient 429s during ramp-up.

nora: Customer also wants a short explanation of scopes so their security team understands least-privilege tokens. I'll attach sample whoami and recommended scope combos.

sam: Sample note: `generate` for text gen, `embeddings` for vector ops; combine when POC needs both. Use time-limited tokens for demos.

eva: Added the one-pager to the ticket and sent to customer. ETA from them to confirm security QA: EOD.

nora: Closing the swarm unless anything else shows up. :thumbsup:
